comparator.name: Bachelor Bedrijfskunde
comparator.sourceNotes: The July 2026 curriculum defines a 180-EC bachelor with a 60-EC first year, 60-EC second year and a 60-EC third year. For year 3, this pathway preserves 30 EC of genuine choice space as a 15-EC minor plus 15 EC of unnamed electives, then includes the compulsory Advanced Research Skills, Methods Master Classes and Cross Cultural Management and instantiates the Entrepreneurship for Growth track (17 EC). Entrepreneurship is selected under the neutral broad-identity rule because the programme explicitly makes entrepreneurship central across the first two years; the choice is not based on UCR fit.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic Bedrijfskunde programme has three formal third-year tracks. Entrepreneurship is explicitly central across the first two years, including venture creation, innovation and growth, so Entrepreneurship for Growth most directly continues the programme-wide academic identity. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two additional generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible after the closest match: Sustainable Business Strategies and Financial Analysis & Investment. Both produce curricula that are substantively distinct and exceed the 30-EC pairwise floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

notes.text: RSM Bedrijfskunde provides a dense compulsory sequence across business functions, including primary processes, HRM, supply-chain management, management accounting and simulation, plus a formal third-year track and bachelor project. UCR can build coherent business, sustainability and finance/analytics programmes, but it does not reproduce the same complete functional sequence or formal track/project structure.
